DEFINITION · qeva:1:negation@1

Negation

Negation forms a statement that denies another statement under the chosen semantics.

editoriallogic

PLAIN

The idea

Negation forms a statement that denies another statement under the chosen semantics.

EXACT

The compact statement

¬ is a unary connective. In classical two-valued semantics, v(¬P)=1 exactly when v(P)=0; constructive semantics gives a different proof-theoretic reading.

EXAMPLE

¬(2=3) denies the equality 2=3.

BOUNDARY / CAVEAT

Double-negation elimination is not valid in every logic.

ASSUMPTIONS

  • The declared propositional language context is fixed.
